Crazy Tube Circuits browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive fuzz browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive overdrive browse by enclosure pedal events 2026 NAMM 2026 Crazy Tube Circuits Orama - Dual Drive Published on December 10, 2025 Crazy Tube Circuits fuzz overdrive pedal NAMM 2026 Information The Crazy Tube Circuits Orama is a dual-drive pedal that merges two independent gain circuits inspired by distinct eras of British tone and boutique fuzz design. It combines a JFET-based amp section modeled after the Orange OR120 amplifier with a powerful fuzz section derived from the Frantone Peach Fuzz . Both circuits can be used independently or stacked, offering a wide tonal range from articulate overdrive to saturated fuzz, designed to embody the full dynamic spectrum of rock and stoner tones. The AMP section captures the full gain range of the Orange OR120, from clean and edge-of-breakup tones to heavily driven distortion. It uses JFET transistors powered by an internal voltage booster that elevates the standard 9V DC input to high-voltage operation, ensuring large headroom, enhanced dynamics, and authentic amp-like response. Key tone-shaping parameters include the F.A.T. (Fatness Adjustment Tweak) , which adjusts low-mid emphasis and gain structure, and H.F.D. (High Frequency Dynamics) , which enhances upper harmonics and presence for added clarity and mix-cutting definition. Additional EQ controls labeled Hz and kHz govern bass and treble frequencies, respectively, while the gain and master controls handle drive intensity and overall output volume. The AMP section's high output level allows it to function effectively as a standalone preamp when used with a power amplifier or cab simulator. The FUZZ section is based on the Frantone Peach Fuzz, a 1990s boutique design that uses amplifier ICs for clipping instead of traditional transistors or diodes, producing a distinctive saturated tone with a thick harmonic character. Its fuzz , tone , and volume controls allow broad sculpting from smooth, rounded fuzz to aggressive, sustaining distortion. A two-way toggle switch provides RAW and BURN voicings: RAW delivers lower gain and tighter bass for vintage-inspired clarity, while BURN increases gain, bass content, and sustain for dense, molten fuzz textures.
